author: Amanda Brennan
title: SEEING DOUBLE: 5 sets of twins graduate high school in Cumberland Co. - NewsBreak
text:
By Amanda Brennan ,
47 minutes ago GREENUP, Ill. (WCIA) — At Cumberland High School, 72 recent graduates are starting their next chapters. 10 of those students are twins! That’s right, five sets of twins who have grown up together are now going their separate ways.
“We don’t really think about it, but to have five sets of us in this small of a town is actually kind of impressive,” Trey Lewis, one of the graduating twins, said with a smile.
Cumberland High School sits just north of Greenup, a village of 1,300 people.
“When we were thinking about graduation, what kind of crowd we were gonna have, well…10 of them share families! So it balanced out with the big numbers,” Daniel Huffman, the school’s principal, said.
As each twin crossed the stage, Todd Hall, the high school civics teacher, proudly read their names. His relationship with each twin and their families dates back to the first day of kindergarten, when he served as the elementary school principal.
Loved ones, coworkers mourn man killed in I-74 construction zone tragedy “When they asked me to read the names, I was like, ‘I can’t say no to this!’ This is the greatest honor,” Hall said. “It means that I meant something, and they meant a lot to me.”
He has watched the youngesters grow up, discover their passions and find their personalities.
“That was a unique class because of the five sets of twins. But it was a great class overall. Just a bunch of good kids in that class,” the educator added.
The students are looking back at their memories together over the years, including Rylan and Camden James, one of the identical sets. One funny moment they say they’ll always remember involved pranking a kindergarten teacher.
“We switched shoes because that was how our teacher told us apart was by the shoes. So we switched them, and she got really confused,” they explained.
Andrej Stojakovic removes name from NBA Draft, set to return to Illini Gaven and Trey Lewis are also identical.
“You have a best buddy, you also have a punching bag once in a while. Okay, don’t say that part,” they joked during the interview. “If you have to learn to share. If you do not, you’re going to have blood baths!”
The other sets of twins are fraternal.
“Half the people don’t even know we’re twins. One of our teachers thought we were cousins,” Jade and Ava Carr said.
Dominik and Maximus Strader liked being separated, while other siblings like Gabriella and Gibson Hutton always wanted to be by each other’s sides. In kindergarten, they had a hard time separating for just a few minutes.
“We both cried, and our teachers had to be like, ‘No, it’s okay! You’ll see each other in ten minutes, it’ll be fine,'” Gabriella said.
20-year-old Effingham man arrested in connection to stabbing Now, the 10 friends are going their separate ways for the very first time. Many of them will attend Lake Land College in Mattoon, and others plan to go to EIU or SIUE.
The Strader twins are going further away, following in their father’s footsteps and serving the U.S. Military.
“I wanted to travel the world. I wanted to see, experience, and meet so many new people,” Dominik said.
No matter where life takes them next, the ten twins have a lifelong bond. Their roads will always lead back to Central Illinois, to the place and people who raised them from young kids getting their footing, to young adults taking big leaps for their futures.
Besides just graduating together, some also share a birthday! Dominik and Maximus, as well as Gaven and Trey, were all born on Nov. 22. They were born six hours apart. Gabriella and Gibson’s birthday is on Oct. 31. A couple of years later, their parents welcomed a younger sister, also born on Oct. 31.
It’s also a milestone year for Mr. Hall; he officially retired at the end of May.
